preconditions.expression: n >= 3 and m >= 2 and m < n
preconditions.description: The number of towns n is at least 3, and the number of monasteries m is at least 2 and strictly less than n.

preconditions.expression: len(monasteries) == m and all(1 <= town <= n for town in monasteries) and len(set(monasteries)) == m
preconditions.description: The monasteries list contains exactly m distinct town indices between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b and 1 <= c <= 1000 for a, b, c in edges)
preconditions.description: The edges form a tree with n-1 bidirectional roads, each with a positive integer length between 1 and 1000.

preconditions.expression: all(a != b for a, b, _ in edges)
preconditions.description: No self-loops exist in the road network.

postconditions.description: The output consists of two integers: the maximum number of pilgrims Walter can make unhappy (max_unhappy) and the number of towns (num_ways) that can be destroyed to achieve this maximum.

postconditions.expression: max_unhappy == max(sum(1 for pilgrim in pilgrims if all(town in pilgrim['farthest'] for town in pilgrim['farthest'] if town not in reachable_from[pilgrim['monastery']][town])) for town in non_monastery_towns)
postconditions.description: max_unhappy is the maximum number of pilgrims that can be made unhappy by destroying exactly one non-monastery town. A pilgrim is unhappy if all monasteries in their farthest list become unreachable from their monastery after the destruction.

postconditions.expression: num_ways == sum(1 for town in non_monastery_towns if sum(1 for pilgrim in pilgrims if all(town in pilgrim['farthest'] for town in pilgrim['farthest'] if town not in reachable_from[pilgrim['monastery']][town])) == max_unhappy)
postconditions.description: num_ways is the count of non-monastery towns whose destruction results in exactly max_unhappy pilgrims being made unhappy.
The maximum number of unhappy pilgrims is between 1 and m (inclusive), as there are m pilgrims.
